## Episode Thesis

The whole episode is an interview with Magnus Söderlind, CEO of Bergman & Beving and a former deputy CEO of Lagercrantz, about how serial acquirers work. He covers the 1982 model of 15% yearly profit growth financed with the company's own money, the target that operating profit be at least 45% of working capital, the traffic-light model for allocating capital across the group's companies, and the three skills needed to run such a company: acquisitions, operations and investor-style capital allocation. He doubts that many of the serial acquirers listed in the zero-rate era will last, says construction and industry have probably bottomed and expects a cautious recovery in 2027. The hosts kept all stock-specific discussion for next week.
